absent: Transport send, receive, retransmit and congestion behavior beyond header and timeout structures.
Credential creation, refresh, binding and GSS context establishment beyond flavor numbers and credential containers.
Pipe filesystem mount, lookup, open, read, write and timeout handling beyond message and pipe layouts.
Server request dispatch, procedure execution and reply generation beyond authentication verdicts and statistics counters.
XDR stream encode and decode traversal across pages, vectors and scatter lists beyond cursor and buffer layouts.
Lock ordering, interrupt context and sleeping rules for wait queues and pipes beyond presence of spinlocks.
Proc filesystem layout and lifetime for statistics beyond inert registration helpers.

findings.text: Authentication flavor carrier is 32-bit unsigned. Core values are NULL 0, UNIX 1, SHORT 2, DES 3, KRB 4, GSS 6, TLS 7 with 5 unassigned, and MAXFLAVOR 8 as upper bound. Pseudo flavors occupy 390003 to 390011: KRB5 variants at 390003-390005, locality-key variants at 390006-390008, SPKM variants at 390009-390011.

Message type assigns CALL 0 and REPLY 1. Reply verdict assigns ACCEPTED 0 and DENIED 1. Accepted status assigns SUCCESS 0, PROG_UNAVAIL 1, PROG_MISMATCH 2, PROC_UNAVAIL 3, GARBAGE_ARGS 4, SYSTEM_ERR 5, plus internal DROP_REPLY 60000. Rejection assigns MISMATCH 0 and AUTH_ERROR 1. Authentication status assigns OK 0 through FAILED 7 in order, and GSS credential versus context problems at 13 and 14.

Size bounds are machine name 255, authentication blob 400 bytes, network name 256, and rpcbind network identifier length 5. Call header base is 6 words and reply header base is 4 words, with authenticated maxima derived by adding credential overhead scaled from the authentication bound. Wire big-endian equivalents exist for zero through two and for call, reply, acceptance and every status above.

Stream framing uses a 32-bit big-endian fragment header where the most significant bit marks the final fragment, its complement masks the length, and the largest representable payload is two to the thirty-first minus one. Rpcbind network identifiers are short tokens udp, tcp, rdma, sctp and their version six forms plus local. Universal address length is built from a short dotted suffix size plus version four or six textual address length, with the generic maximum equal to the version six form.

Task option bits span async through credential-without-reference, including swapper, movable, null credentials, major seen, unreachable fatal, dynamic allocation, no round robin, soft, soft connect, sent, timeout, no connect and no retransmit timeout. Priorities are low minus one, normal zero, high one, privileged two, with queue count derived from that span. Run states enumerate running, queued, active, need transmit, need receive and pin wait. XDR unit is one 32-bit word, network object limit 1024, buffer flags read, write and sparse, and scatter helper size 8.

Pipe filesystem directory head pairs a list of entries with a dentry. Directory object pairs a list node, an operations pointer and opaque data. Its operations offer create and destroy against a directory dentry. Message node pairs a list node, data pointer, total length, copied count and error code. Pipe operations offer upcall, downcall, release, open and message destruction. Pipe carries three lists for queued and in-progress directions, length and reader/writer counts, flags with wait-for-open, delayed timeout work, ops pointer, spinlock and dentry. Inode wrapper pairs the VFS inode, private pointer, pipe pointer and wait queue.

Call message bundles procedure descriptor, argument and result pointers and credential. Wait linkage bundles list, related-task links and timer list. Timeout policy bundles initial, maximum and increment durations, retry limit and exponential flag. Task bundles reference count, operation and RPC result codes, global list node, callback and action pointers, sleep timeout, runstate word, wait queue pointer, a union of work item versus wait linkage, embedded call message, private data and caller callbacks, client, transport, operated credential, request, workqueue, start timestamp, owner identifier, flags, timeout and debug counters, and packed priority plus garbage and credential retry fields. Setup bundle and caller callback table carry creation parameters and prepare, completion, statistics and release hooks.

Wait queue bundles a spinlock, one task list per priority level, maximum and current priority bytes, remaining count for the current selection, total queued length, an embedded timer list, and an optional name when debugging or tracing is enabled. Timer node bundles a list node, expiry instant and delayed work. Round-trip estimator bundles a default timeout plus five slots each of smoothed average, smoothed deviation and consecutive timeout count.

Client statistics bundle program pointer with network, datagram, stream, connect and reconnect counters plus call, retransmit, credential-refresh and garbage counters. Server statistics bundle program pointer with network and call-shape counters plus per-version per-procedure counts held as per-CPU pointers. Service credential bundles user and group identities, group set, flavor, raw and derived principal strings, target principal and mechanism pointer. Authentication domain bundles reference count, hash node, name, flavor operations and RCU head. Authentication operations bundle name, owner, flavor number and accept, release, domain release, client selection and pseudoflavor hooks.

Network object pairs length with byte pointer. XDR buffer pairs header and tail vectors with optional page array, page offset and length, disposition flags, total storage capacity and encoded message length. Array descriptor bundles element size, current and maximum lengths and element codec. Stream cursor bundles current and end pointers, buffer and vector pointers, scratch vector, page cursor plus mapped address, remaining decode words and debugging request pointer. Kernel codec consumes a request and stream.

Pipe helpers expose conversion from VFS inode to wrapper, a predicate reporting whether a message has been partially consumed and detached, two pipe filesystem priority levels with NFS below RPC, and mount versus unmount event identifiers.

Scheduler helpers expose queue-name retrieval with fallback, queue-name assignment with an empty variant when names are unavailable, swap activation reporting invalid argument and empty deactivation, a signaled test on current task state, priority-queue detection from maximum priority, flag predicates for async, swapper, soft, soft-connect, sent and movable, and atomic runstate transitions for running and queued plus activation test.

Statistics registration helpers are inert in these fragments: initialization reports success, exit and unregistration do nothing, registration returns null, zeroing does nothing, and server sequence display does nothing.

Service credential helpers expose initialization clearing group, principal and mechanism fields and release dropping those references before reinitializing. Hash helpers expose string and memory hashing reduced to a requested bit width. Timeout helpers expose bounded update of per-timer miss counts and retrieval of the current miss count, with timer zero meaning no timer.

XDR helpers expose buffer initialization from a start address and length, 64-bit big-endian encode and decode advancing the cursor by two words, network object duplication with caller-supplied allocation mode, vector length adjustment from a cursor, array encoding as opaque bytes, and unaligned big-endian 64-bit store and load.

A message counts as in flight only after some bytes were copied and it left its queue. Buffer initialization points the header at caller storage, empties tail and paging, clears flags and encoded length, and records capacity equal to supplied length. Queue name lookup tolerates null queue or missing name. Priority queue detection requires positive maximum priority. Miss-count updates decrement toward a lower request, cap an upper request at eight, and ignore timer zero.

Each wait queue carries its own spinlock alongside the per-priority task lists, selection state, total length and timer list, so queue mutation and selection are serialized by that lock. Each pipe carries its own spinlock alongside its three message lists, length and reader/writer counts, so list and counter updates are serialized by that lock. Task runstate uses atomic bit operations for running, queued and active transitions.

Server authentication verdicts progress through garbage, valid, negative, okay, drop, close, denied, pending and complete states. Task execution uses runstate bits for running, queued, active, need transmit, need receive and pin wait, with queued and running manipulated as separate atomic flags. Task option flags record lifecycle facts such as sent, major timeout seen, soft versus timeout failure mode, and movable versus pinned transport affinity.

The signaled predicate names a fixed outer task identifier instead of its parameter, so it does not test the supplied task when names differ. Authenticated header maxima and object bounds are fixed at compile time, so oversized credentials, machine names or network objects cannot be represented. Fragment length excludes its marker bit, limiting payloads to signed 31-bit range. Universal address maxima inherit external textual address lengths, and swap activation always fails in these fragments.
